passages.title: What Is FORTRESS? Pentagon’s 90-Day Plan to Keep US Military Bases Running
passages.passage:
Most U.S. military bases will need to be able to run independently for at least three months should they be cut off from external supplies in the event of a conflict, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote in a recent memo.
Hegseth unveiled the so-called Federal Operations for Resilience, Troop Resources, Energy, Supply, and Survivability (FORTRESS) initiative on September 30, dubbing it "the nation's insurance policy" to make sure the U.S. would still be able to obtain the materials it needs and carry out operations if traditional supply chains were cut off.
U.S. military bases will be prepared to keep functioning without external support for at least 90 days as part of this plan, Fox News Digital reported on Sunday.
This includes keeping electricity flowing, having enough fuel and water to operate and being able to communicate for military operations, even if civilian infrastructure is taken out, according to the report, which added that all major U.S. military facilities in the continental U.S. will be held to this 90-day standard.

passages.title: 'It's an Intolerable Risk': Pentagon Reportedly Prepares US Military for 90 Days Without Civilian Infrastructure
passages.passage:
The Pentagon is preparing major US military bases to remain without outside support for at least 90 days, Fox News Digital reported.
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the wider initiative on 30 September, promising more independent power supplies and stronger protections for military installations.
'Power is combat now,' Parnell told Fox News Digital. The Pentagon's reported proposals include portable nuclear reactors, large battery systems, and microgrids capable of operating independently of civilian electricity networks.
FORTRESS also looks beyond the bases themselves. According to Fox News Digital, the strategy calls for reserves of ammunition, fuel, medical supplies, electronics and other essential materials. Critical requirements would have at least two qualified supply or production routes to limit dependence on a single provider.
The Pentagon has not published a complete implementation schedule or demonstrated that the reported 90-day standard is achievable at every major installation. Even the costs will depend on what individual bases need, from independent electricity generation to fuel storage and communications resilience.

passages.title: Why Balochistan observes August 11 as its 'Independence Day': The history behind the date
passages.passage:
Why Balochistan observes August 11 as its 'Independence Day': The history behind the date
In light of renewed debates and discussions about Balochistan within the politics of South Asia, there is a certain date that comes to prominence on a regular basis: August 11. Each year, numerous Baloch national movements celebrate this day as the Independence Day of Balochistan, because it denotes the brief period of time when the Khanate of Kalat existed as an independent state prior to joining Pakistan.
Recently, Baloch representative and diplomat Mir Yar Baloch took to X (formerly Twitter) and shared, "The Republic of Balochistan announces worldwide celebrations of August 11 as the Independence Day of Balochistan with national unity."
While the Baloch nationalists observe August 11 as marking the day of independence for their land, Pakistan claims the legitimacy of its accession in 1948.

In a statement, the Republic of Balochistan called on the international community to recognise what it described as an independent and sovereign Balochistan, while urging people across the Baloch nation to commemorate the day with unity.
According to the statement, the Republic of Balochistan regards August 11 as its Independence Day and said the occasion would be observed every year.

A strong earthquake of magnitude 6.4 jolted Japan’s Ishikawa and other central Japan prefectures on Tuesday, the country’s weather agency said.
According to the preliminary information, the earthquake occurred at a depth of around 10 km off the western coast of the prefecture measuring a lower 5 on the Japanese seismic scale of 7 in Ishkiwara’s Noto, a region which is still recovering from the deadly January 1 earthquakes.
The Japanese Meteorological Agency (JMA) had said that at least 155 earthquakes along with the aforementioned 7.5-magnitude earthquake (and the 6-magnitude aftershock that followed closely after) struck Japan on January 1.
The massive earthquake had toppled buildings, triggered landslides and sparked a massive fire. Video footage shared on social media and also shared by Japanese local news outlets showed restaurant doors and street signs shaking due to the intensity of the earthquake. At a karaoke bar in Ishikawa, people were heard crying for help as tables were recorded shaking intensely following the earthquake, spilling drinks from glasses.

passages.title: 5.7-magnitude earthquake hits central Japan, injuring at least 20
passages.passage:
At least 20 people were injured after a 5.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Japan early on Sunday, local media reported.
Kyodo News reported injuries in Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures, citing local authorities.
The earthquake originated in the western part of Shizuoka prefecture at a depth of about 40 kilometres (25 miles), according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.
The quake was the strongest to hit Aichi in about three decades.
A 4.3 magnitude earthquake hit the Kumamoto prefecture in southwestern Japan on Sunday morning.
Japan, which sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire and directly atop four major tectonic plates, is one of the most seismically active countries in the world.

A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck central Japan early Sunday, injuring dozens of residents and causing widespread transit delays across key transportation corridors. The tremor occurred at 1:04 a.m.
local time on Sunday, November 8, 2026 (16:04 GMT on Saturday, November 7), according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.
Local authorities across Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures reported that at least 20 to 24 people sustained injuries during the shaking. Officials noted that the injuries primarily resulted from falls, accidents on stairs, and individuals tumbling from their beds as the ground shook in the middle of the night.
The earthquake temporarily disrupted high-speed rail operations in Japan's central economic corridor. The Tokaido Shinkansen bullet train operated at reduced speeds between Shizuoka and Gifu-Hashima while personnel conducted track and safety inspections, before returning to normal-speed service before noon on Sunday.

passages.title: At Least 20 Injured After Magnitude 5.7 Earthquake Hits Central Japan

It registered a maximum intensity of 5-upper on Japan's seismic intensity scale in parts of Aichi Prefecture.Strong shaking was also recorded in parts of Shizuoka, Aichi, Gifu and Nagano prefectures, while long-period ground motion of Level 1 was observed in parts of Nagano and Aichi, according to the JMA.No tsunami warning was issued following the earthquake.The quake disrupted some local train services, while other services were operated at reduced speeds as a precautionary measure.Japan is highly prone to earthquakes because it lies along the Pacific Ring of Fire. passages.title: George W. Bush's Brother Says Donald Trump Has Done 'Enormous Damage' to GOP as He Votes Against MAGA Pick Ken Paxton in Texas Senate Race
passages.passage:
Neil Bush, the 71-year-old younger brother of former President George W. Bush and son of former President George H.W. Bush, has launched a sharp attack on President Donald Trump and broken party lines to vote against Trump’s handpicked candidate, Ken Paxton, in the Texas U.S. Senate race.
Bush revealed in a Facebook post on Tuesday, October 20, that he cast an early ballot for Democratic candidate James Talarico, 37, instead of the Trump-endorsed Republican incumbent.
“I have been a Republican for most of my life, and I still believe deeply in many traditional Republican principles,” Bush wrote in his deliberate Facebook post. “But character matters more than party affiliation.”
Bush praised Talarico, saying, “I’ve never met James Talarico, but I have been enormously impressed by the way he approaches complicated and controversial issues."
The announcement follows reports that other family members, including George W. Bush's daughter Barbara Bush, 44, have financially supported Talarico’s campaign to flip the Texas Senate seat.
If Talarico wins, he would be the first Democrat to win a statewide race in Texas in 32 years.

passages.title: George W. Bush’s brother blasts Trump in rare political message: ‘Deeply troubled’
passages.passage:
George W. Bush’s brother blasts Trump in rare political message: ‘Deeply troubled’
The brother of former President George W. Bush issued a rare political statement on Tuesday, weighing in on the Texas Senate race.
Neil Bush said in a Facebook post that he voted for Democratic candidate James Talarico in the race for the U.S. Senate seat in Texas. He acknowledged that he has “never” posted a political message on Facebook before now.
Bush criticized Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, saying that he is “deeply troubled” by his conduct and decision to challenge the results of the 2020 election. President Donald Trump endorsed Paxton over incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in the GOP primary race despite the state official’s mounting controversies.
“I’ve never met James Talarico, but I have been enormously impressed by the way he approaches complicated and controversial issues,” Bush wrote.
Fox News Digital reported that Barbara Bush, the daughter of George W. Bush, also appeared to support Talarico. According to Fox News, she donated $2,500 to the main PAC supporting Talarico’s campaign.

passages.title: United Nations: 81st General Assembly opens in New York
passages.passage:
United Nations: 81st General Assembly opens in New York
The atmosphere is one of “an era of profound uncertainty,” in the words of UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, as the 81st United Nations General Assembly opens its debate on Tuesday, September 22. Heads of state and government from around the world are taking part, addressing international challenges ranging from security and geopolitical tensions to economic issues and artificial intelligence.
Expectations are generally realistic, with few anticipating any major breakthroughs. There is, however, considerable attention on what will happen away from the spotlight of the General Assembly chamber—namely, the bilateral meetings focused on the ongoing conflicts. A meeting between UN Secretary-General Guterres and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov is already scheduled for September 24.
For the first time in its history, the General Assembly has also placed artificial intelligence at the top of its agenda—seeking a global agreement to establish limits on its development and use. Guterres has included AI among the “three existential threats” of our time, alongside the climate crisis and growing inequality.

passages.title: Pope Leo XIV confirms on the flight to Uruguay that he voted in the U.S. legislative elections: "I am proud to be American"
passages.passage: Pope Leo XIV confirmed this Friday, during the flight from Rome to Montevideo that marked the start of his sixth apostolic journey, that he voted in the United States legislative elections. Asked by American journalists, the Pope replied: «I have already made a statement on this; I am proud to be American and to exercise the right to vote». He also explained that he did not vote in the Peruvian elections, of which he is also a citizen, because there was no technical possibility of doing so from abroad, and added that, had he been able, he would have done so, because «it is a good thing». According to Vatican News, the Pontiff voted by mail.

On Saturday the Iran‑aligned Houthis announced a series of missile and drone assaults aimed at Saudi Arabia’s Aramco oil installations and the main airport in Riyadh, alongside strikes on Saudi military positions near the Yemen border.
The group’s military spokesman, Yahya Saree, posted on X that six coordinated operations were executed, hitting both energy assets and transport hubs. The attacks were described as targeting “Saudi troops and infrastructure” on both sides of the frontier.
